jobs_results.description:
About the Role  


At Freestone Grove, the fundamental research process is built on bottom-up, firm-specific analysis within deep sector specialization. We believe that specialization compounds, and that using alternative data and modern quantitative methods to produce actionable insight is a core component of the investment approach. Each sector has its own nuances and machinery, and we are building a team of researchers who will master them. 


Early-career researchers join a central team that serves every sector we cover, which means unusually broad exposure in the first year: you will work across 1-2 sectors including but not limited to healthcare, financials, technology, and industrials on live questions posed by the investors covering them. As you build technical depth, sector knowledge, and commercial judgment, the path is toward dedicated coverage of a sector of your own. 


The work is turning large, complex, and often unconventional datasets into differentiated single-name insight. Working directly with portfolio managers and analysts, you will construct economically and statistically grounded forecasting models of firm-specific, industry, and macroeconomic fundamentals. You will be expected to reach conclusions, size your confidence in them, and defend them to the people who will act on the work. The premium throughout is on process, robustness, interpretability, and economic significance. 


We are looking for curious, rigorous thinkers with a genuine interest in markets and in how businesses actually make money, ready to challenge assumptions and push the boundaries of applied data science in a fast-paced, early-stage setting. 


The day-to-day responsibilities will include: 



Working on research projects, independently and collaboratively, across the sectors our investment teams cover 


Working closely with our Head of Data Science and Head of Quantitative Strategies, alongside highly talented sector-specific fundamental investment professionals 


Sourcing, cleaning, and exploring new datasets including alternative, transactional, regulatory, and firm-disclosed 


Building forecasting models of firm-specific, industry, and macroeconomic fundamentals, grounded in the economics of the business 


Measuring the predictive content of a dataset for a specific single-name or sector question, and testing investment hypotheses against it 


Investigating anomalies, reconciling conflicting sources, monitoring data pipelines, and documenting assumptions and limitations 


Building and maintaining investor-facing trackers, dashboards, and recurring research workflows 


Improving the quality, testing, documentation, and reusability of the shared Python and SQL tooling used across the team 


Presenting research findings to portfolio managers, analysts, and quantitative researchers, and defending them 

Attributes 



Intellectual curiosity, particularly about how businesses operate and make money 


Attention to detail, and the instinct to check a result before presenting it 


Solid grounding in mathematics and statistics, and the discipline to represent uncertainty honestly rather than assume it away 


Impeccable written and verbal communication, with the ability to communicate complex ideas to colleagues, both quantitative and non-quantitative 


Ownership mentality, and comfort building process rather than inheriting it 


Ability to work efficiently both independently and within a team, and to prioritize competing requests under tight deadlines 

Qualifications 



Bachelor's or advanced degree in a quantitative field such as statistics, mathematics, physics, astronomy, computer science, economics, or financial engineering 


Strong working proficiency in Python, including pandas and the standard scientific stack 


Proficiency of SQL, with familiarity with version control, testing, and writing code that colleagues will read and reuse 


Comfortable collaborating through git and working with APIs 


Recent or soon-to-be graduate through approximately four years of experience in quantitative research, data science, analytics, or software engineering

Familiarity with company financial statements, industry KPIs, or alternative datasets is a plus
